title: Document security guarantees and supported workflows
lead: Keep the project, CLI, and package documentation consistent about manifest protection, deterministic-token guarantees, safe credential inputs, compatibility, and intended use of generated datasets.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Security and workflow guidance is repeated across project, CLI, and package readmes; changes to credentials, token behavior, and compatibility need consistent user-facing instructions.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: Add or update documentation checks only if the repository already has a suitable mechanism; otherwise use a manual cross-document review.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: After ob-01–ob-05 settle behavior, align descriptions of manifest protection defaults, safe credential inputs, deterministic-token guarantees and limits, compatibility/migration, and synthetic data use. Keep examples executable and secret-free.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Search all documentation for stale claims/options and compare examples with current CLI help and public APIs. Run the existing package/CLI smoke workflow when code changes are included.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Update all affected readmes together and keep example secrets obviously non-production.
